style: Bengali Aatchala (sloped eight-roofed vernacular temple style)
key_structures: Kalika sanctum with Bengali double aatchala roof
Jor Bangla on the approach to the sanctum
Natmandir immediately south of the sanctum
Shyam Rai Mandir and swing pavilion on the west
Sosthi Tala and four mapped Shiva lingam shrines
Harkath Tala near the south end of the court
special_features: Curved chala cornice reflecting thatched roof Bengali vernacular heritage
Iconic black touchstone image of Maa Kali with three golden eyes, protruding golden tongue, and four hands
Kundupukur sacred pond east of the main enclosure
materials: White lime plaster and stucco work
period: Present temple documented in the early 19th century
renovation_history: The present shrine is associated with the Sabarna Roy Choudhury family. The Natmandir and Shyam Rai Mandir were added in the 19th century.
